table.name: circuits
table.purpose: F1 circuits reference table: one row per racing circuit, with location, country, geographic coordinates and a Wikipedia link. Referenced by races, lap times, pit stops and results.

col_001.name: circuitId
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier of the circuit, referenced by races, lapTimes, pitStops and results.

col_002.name: circuitRef
col_002.description: Unique short slug/reference name of the circuit (e.g. 'ricard', 'zolder'), used as a stable textual key.

col_003.name: name
col_003.description: Full display name of the circuit (e.g. 'Circuit Paul Ricard', 'Silverstone Circuit').

col_004.name: location
col_004.description: Town/city or locality where the circuit is situated (e.g. 'Le Castellet', 'Heusden-Zolder'); some values are regions like 'California'.

col_006.name: lat
col_006.description: Latitude of the circuit in decimal degrees (range -34.9 to 57.3, consistent with world-wide circuit locations).

col_007.name: lng
col_007.description: Longitude of the circuit in decimal degrees (range -118.2 to 138.9, consistent with world-wide circuit locations).

col_009.name: url
col_009.description: Wikipedia URL of the circuit's page.

table.name: constructorResults
table.purpose: Per-race championship points earned by each constructor (Formula 1). One row per constructor per race, recording the points that constructor scored in that race (with a 'D' flag for disqualified results).

col_001.name: constructorResultId
col_001.description: Surrogate primary key uniquely identifying each constructor-per-race result row.

col_002.name: raceId
col_002.description: Reference to the race (races table) in which the constructor scored these points.

col_003.name: constructorId
col_003.description: Reference to the constructor (constructors table) that scored these points.

col_004.name: points
col_004.description: Championship points scored by the constructor in that race. Mostly 0 (many races with no points), max 66.

col_005.name: status
col_005.description: Result status flag; the only observed value is 'D', almost certainly meaning disqualified. Null for normal results.

table.name: constructorStandings
table.purpose: Formula 1 constructor (team) championship standings after each race: one row per constructor per race, with cumulative points, position, and win count at that point in the season.

col_001.name: constructorStandingId
col_001.description: Surrogate primary key, unique per row.

col_002.name: raceId
col_002.description: Reference to races.col_001; the race after which this standing snapshot applies.

col_003.name: constructorId
col_003.description: Reference to constructors.col_001; the team this standing belongs to.

col_004.name: points
col_004.description: Cumulative championship points for the constructor at that point in the season; half values (e.g. 27.5, 72.5) reflect historical shared/split point awards.

col_005.name: position
col_005.description: Constructor's championship position after that race (1 = leading); max 22 matches number of constructors in a season.

col_006.name: positionText
col_006.description: Position rendered as text (VARCHAR but numeric values); duplicates col_005.

col_007.name: wins
col_007.description: Cumulative number of race wins by that constructor so far in the season; mostly 0.

table.name: constructors
table.purpose: Formula 1 constructors (racing teams/car builders). One row per constructor, referenced by results, constructorResults, constructorStandings, qualifying.

col_001.name: constructorId
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier of the constructor, referenced by results, constructorResults, constructorStandings and qualifying.

col_002.name: constructorRef
col_002.description: Unique slug-style reference code for the constructor (lowercase, hyphenated, e.g. 'cooper-borgward', 'tyrrell').

col_004.name: nationality
col_004.description: Constructor's nationality as an adjective (British, American, Italian, ...).

table.name: driverStandings
table.purpose: Formula 1 championship standings for each driver after each race: cumulative points, championship position, and win count per driver per race.

col_001.name: driverStandingsId
col_001.description: Surrogate primary key uniquely identifying each driver-standing row.

col_002.name: raceId
col_002.description: Reference to races; the race up to (and including) which the standings are cumulative. 970 distinct races.

col_003.name: driverId
col_003.description: Reference to drivers; the driver this standing row belongs to.

col_004.name: points
col_004.description: Cumulative championship points accumulated by the driver up to that race. Half values (e.g. 27.5) reflect shared/half points awarded in F1.

col_005.name: position
col_005.description: Driver's championship standing position after that race (1 = leader). Each of positions 1-5 appears exactly 970 times, once per race.

col_006.name: positionText
col_006.description: Championship position stored as text; duplicates col_005 (VARCHAR-typed copy of the position).

col_007.name: wins
col_007.description: Number of races the driver has won so far in the season (cumulative win count).

table.name: drivers
table.purpose: Formula 1 drivers reference table: one row per driver, with identity, permanent race number, driver code, date of birth, nationality and Wikipedia link. Referenced by results, driverStandings, lapTimes, pitStops and qualifying.

col_001.name: driverId
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier for each driver, referenced by results, driverStandings, lapTimes, pitStops and qualifying.

col_002.name: driverRef
col_002.description: Unique slug/short reference for the driver (surname-based, e.g. 'gilles_villeneuve'), used as a stable textual key.

col_003.name: number
col_003.description: Permanent driver race number (2-99). Null for ~96% of rows, i.e. mostly for drivers who raced before permanent numbers were introduced.

col_004.name: code
col_004.description: Three-letter driver broadcast code (e.g. VER, ROS, SAI). Null for ~90% of rows (older drivers).

col_008.name: nationality
col_008.description: Driver's nationality as an adjective (British, American, Italian, ...), including hyphenated dual nationalities.

col_009.name: url
col_009.description: Wikipedia URL for the driver; empty string for one row.

table.name: lapTimes
table.purpose: Per-lap timing for each driver in each race (Formula 1 data): one row per driver per lap, giving lap number, race position at that lap, and lap time in text and milliseconds.

col_001.name: raceId
col_001.description: Identifier of the race; references races.col_001. Many lap rows per race.

col_002.name: driverId
col_002.description: Identifier of the driver; references drivers.col_001.

col_003.name: lap
col_003.description: Lap number within the race (1 to 78, matching the longest F1 races). The statistical join to circuits.col_001 is spurious — this is a lap counter, not a circuit reference.

col_004.name: position
col_004.description: Driver's race position at the end of that lap (1–24, matching typical F1 grid size).

col_005.name: time
col_005.description: Lap time formatted as m:ss.mmm (e.g. '1:31.255' = 1 minute 31.255 seconds).

col_006.name: milliseconds
col_006.description: Lap time in milliseconds; numeric equivalent of col_005 (e.g. 91255 ms = 1:31.255).

table.name: pitStops
table.purpose: Formula 1 pit stop records: one row per pit stop made by a driver during a race, with the lap, local time of day, and stop duration.

col_001.name: raceId
col_001.description: Identifier of the race in which the pit stop occurred; references races.col_001.

col_002.name: driverId
col_002.description: Identifier of the driver who made the pit stop; references drivers.col_001.

col_003.name: stop
col_003.description: Pit stop number for that driver in the race (1st stop, 2nd stop, etc.; values 1-6).

col_004.name: lap
col_004.description: Lap number of the race on which the pit stop occurred (1-74). The statistical join to circuits.col_001 is spurious - lap numbers merely overlap circuit ids; the values are lap counts, not circuit references.

col_005.name: time
col_005.description: Local time of day (HH:MM:SS) at which the pit stop took place during the race.

col_006.name: duration
col_006.description: Pit stop duration in seconds, stored as text with millisecond precision (e.g. '30.888' = 30.888 s).

col_007.name: milliseconds
col_007.description: Pit stop duration in milliseconds (numeric form of col_006; e.g. 30888 ms = 30.888 s). The max of 2011266 ms (~33.5 min) is an outlier, likely a red-flag/very long stop.

table.name: qualifying
table.purpose: Formula 1 qualifying session results: one row per driver per race, with their grid position and lap times for each qualifying segment (Q1, Q2, Q3).

col_001.name: qualifyId
col_001.description: Primary key; unique identifier for the qualifying result row.

col_002.name: raceId
col_002.description: Reference to races(raceId); the race the qualifying session belongs to.

col_003.name: driverId
col_003.description: Reference to drivers(driverId); the driver who set the qualifying times.

col_004.name: constructorId
col_004.description: Reference to constructors(constructorId); the team the driver drove for in that qualifying session.

col_005.name: number
col_005.description: Driver's car number for that race/season (0-99, e.g. 40, 29, 33).

col_006.name: position
col_006.description: Grid/qualifying position the driver achieved (1-28, with 1 most frequent at 339 occurrences, consistent with one pole-sitter per race).

col_007.name: q1
col_007.description: Best lap time in qualifying segment Q1, formatted m:ss.mmm; null when the driver did not set a Q1 time.

col_008.name: q2
col_008.description: Best lap time in qualifying segment Q2, formatted m:ss.mmm; null (51.5%) when the driver was eliminated in or before Q1 and set no Q2 time.

col_009.name: q3
col_009.description: Best lap time in qualifying segment Q3, formatted m:ss.mmm; null (71%) when the driver did not reach Q3.

table.name: races
table.purpose: One row per Formula 1 Grand Prix race (1950-2017), identifying each race, its season, round, circuit, name, date, scheduled start time, and Wikipedia link. Referenced by results, qualifying, lap times, pit stops, and standings tables.

col_001.name: race_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier for each race. Referenced by results, qualifying, lapTimes, pitStops, driverStandings, constructorStandings, constructorResults.

col_002.name: year
col_002.description: Season year of the race (1950-2017); references seasons table (season year).

col_003.name: round
col_003.description: Round number of the race within its season (1-21); each season has one race per round value.

col_004.name: circuit_id
col_004.description: Reference to circuits table identifying the circuit where the race was held.

col_005.name: race_name
col_005.description: Official name of the Grand Prix, e.g. 'British Grand Prix', 'Monaco Grand Prix'.

col_006.name: race_date
col_006.description: Date of the race (1950-05-13 to 2017-11-26), stored as text in YYYY-MM-DD format.

col_007.name: race_time
col_007.description: Scheduled start time of the race (HH:MM:SS, likely local or UTC). Null for 75% of rows, mostly older races where start time is unknown.

col_008.name: race_wiki_url
col_008.description: Wikipedia article URL for the race, one per race.

table.name: results
table.purpose: Race results: one row per driver per race, with grid position, finishing position, points, laps, time/gap, fastest-lap data and finishing status (F1-style data, Ergast schema).

col_001.name: result_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the results table; unique surrogate id per result row.

col_002.name: race_id
col_002.description: Reference to races table; identifies which race this result belongs to.

col_003.name: driver_id
col_003.description: Reference to drivers table; the driver who achieved this result.

col_004.name: constructor_id
col_004.description: Reference to constructors table; the team the driver raced for in this race.

col_005.name: number
col_005.description: Driver/car number used in that race (values up to 208, many distinct). The statistical join to status is spurious; the value range and distribution fit a car number, not a status code.

col_006.name: grid
col_006.description: Starting grid position (0 = started from pit lane, max 34 matches largest grids).

col_007.name: position
col_007.description: Official finishing position as a number; null when the driver did not finish (DNF/DQ), explaining the ~44.5% null rate.

col_008.name: position_text
col_008.description: Finishing position as text: numeric string for classified finishers, 'R' for retired, 'F' and other letters for non-classified outcomes.

col_009.name: position_order
col_009.description: Finishing order as a dense integer rank (no nulls, always populated even for non-finishers).

col_010.name: points
col_010.description: Championship points scored in this race (0 for most, up to 50, e.g. with bonus points).

col_011.name: laps
col_011.description: Number of laps completed by the driver in this race (0 = did not start/lap).

col_012.name: time
col_012.description: Finishing time or gap to the winner as text, e.g. '+8:22.19', '+0.7'; null for the winner and non-finishers.

col_013.name: milliseconds
col_013.description: Finishing time/gap in milliseconds (numeric counterpart of col_012); null rate matches it.

col_014.name: fastest_lap
col_014.description: Lap number on which the driver set their fastest lap (null for most older races where lap data is absent). The 'circuits' join is a spurious coincidence of id ranges.

col_015.name: fastest_lap_rank
col_015.description: Rank of the driver's fastest lap within the race (1 = fastest); null where fastest-lap data is absent.

col_016.name: fastest_lap_time
col_016.description: Fastest lap time as m:ss.mmm text; null where unavailable.

col_017.name: fastest_lap_speed
col_017.description: Average speed of the fastest lap in km/h (values ~90-257); null where unavailable.

col_018.name: status_id
col_018.description: Reference to status table; code for how the race ended for the driver (1 = finished/complete, others = accident, engine, etc.).

table.name: seasons
table.purpose: Formula 1 championship seasons, one row per year from 1950 to 2017, referenced by the races table.

col_001.name: year
col_001.description: Championship season year (1950-2017), primary key; each races row belongs to one season year.

col_002.name: url
col_002.description: Wikipedia URL for that season's Formula One championship article.

table.name: status
table.purpose: Lookup table of race finish/retirement status codes (e.g. finished, +N laps, mechanical failures) referenced by results and driverStandings tables in an F1 database.

col_001.name: statusId
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier for each status code.

col_002.name: status
col_002.description: Human-readable race status label: either a finishing classification relative to the winner ('+1 Lap', '+30 Laps') or a retirement reason ('Engine', 'Out of fuel', 'Fuel rig', 'Water pipe', 'Exhaust').
